chunks: And whatever is in it from Muhammad ibn Sahl, I have narrated it from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Al-Yasa' Al-Ashari.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to the narrator's father, a common scholarly reference.
key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, a well-known narrator in the Four Books.
key_terms.الْأَشْعَرِيُّ: Al-Ashari, a nisba indicating tribal or familial affiliation.
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: May Allah be pleased with them, a phrase of respect used for the two individuals mentioned.
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a prominent companion of the Imams and narrator.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَهْلٍ: Muhammad ibn Sahl, a key narrator in Shia hadith literature.

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Muhammad ibn Sahl in this hadith?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous isnad verification characteristic of Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, where the compiler explicitly links his own transmission to his father, Shaykh al-Mufid, to establish a continuous chain of authority. By tracing the lineage through prominent figures like Sa'd ibn Abdullah and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa to Muhammad ibn Sahl, it underscores the reliability of the Ash'ari school of hadith narrators in Twelver Shia scholarship.
